subject: fix(ingest-content): emit the full JSON shape for an empty corpus
prompt: Running `neuralmind ingest-content <dir> --json` on a directory with no .md or .txt files prints a JSON object with only a few keys (success, files_processed, files_skipped, total_chunks, total_nodes, errors, message). A run that finds files returns many more: project_path, content_only, incremental, files_total, chunks_embedded, orphans_removed, chunk_size, overlap, wall_time_seconds, embed_time_seconds and timed_out. My script parses that documented shape and crashes with a KeyError on an empty directory. The empty case should emit every key a normal run does, with zero or empty values.

subject: fix: neuralmind doctor exits 1 when a check fails, as documented (#624)
prompt: Our CI step runs NeuralMind's health-check subcommand (the one that prints each check as [OK]/[WARN]/[FAIL]) and gates on its exit status, but it always exits 0, even when a check fails. For example, on a project that hasn't been built yet the code-graph check reports FAIL, in both the normal and --json modes. The docs say it exits 1 when any check fails, after printing its report or JSON, and that warnings alone still exit 0. Separately, after NeuralMind automatically recovers an unreadable turbovec index (it renames the old file to index.tvim.stale and writes a fresh index.tvim), the "Turbovec compatibility" check keeps reporting FAIL even though the rebuilt index works. It should report OK when the live index can be read, mention the leftover index.tvim.stale backup in its detail, still FAIL when the live index can't be read, and never rename, rebuild or delete index files while checking.

subject: fix: MCP auth bypass, token persistence, cache cleanup, env var lazy load
prompt: An MCP client can call a NeuralMind tool such as neuralmind_query without any project_path argument, or with project_path set to an empty string or null, and the call runs without any role or permission check, so the RBAC policy is bypassed just by leaving the path out. Such a call should be refused instead: it should return a JSON error whose code is "invalid_request" and whose error message mentions project_path.

subject: fix: anchor the sk- patterns and redact on every backend, not just chroma
prompt: Two problems with credential redaction. First, `neuralmind build --redact-secrets` (NEURALMIND_REDACT_SECRETS=1) only scrubs the text it indexes on the ChromaDB store: on the default turbovec store and on the in_memory store, a node whose label contains an Anthropic API key is embedded with the key verbatim. On every store, the indexed text should have the key replaced by [REDACTED:anthropic-api-key] when redaction is on, and be left untouched when it's off. Second, the redaction applied to cached Bash output shreds ordinary text: `sk-` inside words like task-, disk-, risk-, mask-, desk-, flask-, dask- and brisk- is taken as the start of an OpenAI or Anthropic key, so `git checkout feature/task-management-refactor-v2` comes back as `git checkout feature/ta[REDACTED:openai-api-key]`, and pod names, package names and branch names are mangled the same way. A key shape glued onto the end of a longer identifier (like `deploybotsk-ant-api03-...`) shouldn't be reported as a key, while real keys that start at a word boundary must still be caught.

subject: fix(mcp): grant default roles the progressive-retrieval memory tools (#568)
prompt: Through NeuralMind's MCP tools, calls to neuralmind_memory_search, neuralmind_memory_timeline and neuralmind_memory_get always come back with code "security_denied": with no role given (which means builder), and with role "builder" or "reader". The Memory Layer docs say both default roles can use these read-only memory tools. They should run for builder and reader by default. Writing decisions should stay builder-only, and the admin-only tools should stay admin-only.

subject: fix: boundary-aware prefilter, label-paired PEM, and honest invariants
prompt: `neuralmind scan-for-secrets` pairs private-key markers by position instead of by key type. Text with `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`, a body line, then `-----END EC PRIVATE KEY-----` is reported as a private-key-block finding, although the two markers don't belong together; it should report nothing. Worse, that mismatched pair consumes the range, so a genuine `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- ... -----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----` block right after it is missed. A BEGIN should only pair with an END of the same key type, so that combined input should give exactly one private-key-block finding, and matched RSA, OPENSSH, EC, DSA and PGP blocks should still be found.

subject: fix: merge overlapping spans so no credential fragment survives redaction
prompt: Credential redaction leaves part of a password in the clear. For a line like `export password=redis://default:pa;ssw0rdLongEnough@cache:6379` (the same with `credentials=` or `api_key=`), the redacted output is `export password=[REDACTED:generic-secret-assignment];ssw0rdLongEnough@cache:6379`: the generic assignment match stops at the `;` (likewise at a `,` or a quote), and the rest of the password survives. Overlapping detections should be combined so that no fragment of the password remains, and the result should be a single [REDACTED:connection-string-password] finding. A key that is already fully inside another match shouldn't get a second marker, and the surrounding non-secret text must stay as it is.

subject: fix: detect PREFIX_PASSWORD names and PGP private-key blocks
prompt: `neuralmind scan-for-secrets` reports a .env file full of `DB_PASSWORD="<long random value>"` lines as clean. Assignments whose keyword has a prefix joined by an underscore, such as db_password, DB_PASSWORD, MYSQL_PASSWORD, app_secret, PROD_API_KEY, my_access_token and SERVICE_AUTH_TOKEN, are never flagged, while a plain `password = "..."` is. They should be reported as generic-secret-assignment findings. A keyword glued onto letters (mypassword, thesecret, notoken) and named-but-empty placeholders (`DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}`, `api_key: changeme`) should still not count. The scan also misses PGP private keys: a `-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK----- ... -----END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----` block isn't reported, while RSA, OPENSSH, EC, DSA and ENCRYPTED keys are reported as private-key-block.

subject: fix: GHCR :latest follows the newest release; the session recap breaks ties by mtime (#594)
prompt: When two earlier sessions in a project recorded their last activity at exactly the same timestamp (easy on Windows, where the clock ticks about every 15.6 ms), the "where we left off" summary that NeuralMind shows when a new session starts picks one of them by directory listing order, so the choice is effectively arbitrary. This made a pruning test flaky on Windows CI. On a tie, it should pick the session whose record file was modified most recently, and fall back to the file name only after that, so the newer session wins whichever name sorts first.

subject: fix(security): never ingest dot-files (.env secrets leak); correct gitignore semantics (v4.3.3) (#535)
prompt: Ingesting a folder of documents (`neuralmind ingest <dir>`) ingests dot-files as content: a .env file with `OPENAI_API_KEY=...` ends up verbatim in the index, and .gitignore gets ingested too. Dot-files should never be ingested, while ordinary files like readme.md still are. The .gitignore patterns used to decide what to skip are also matched with the wrong semantics: `docs/*.md` also skips docs/ch1/intro.md (a single `*` shouldn't cross a `/`), a rooted pattern like `/vendor/` matches nothing (it should skip vendor/lib.md but not src/vendor/lib.md), and `**/build_artifacts` matches nothing (it should match both build_artifacts/foo.txt and nested/build_artifacts/x.txt). The rest of the usual gitignore behaviour should keep working, so `build/` skips build/out.js but not build.py, and `temp*` skips temporary/file.md but not attempt/file.md.

subject: fix(D3): DeepSeek QA patches — 4 issues
prompt: When I generate the offline reference answers for the public benchmark's LLM grading from the benchmark_queries_*.json fixtures, the TypeScript fixture's entries come out under the language "ts", taken from the file name benchmark_queries_ts.json, instead of "typescript", which is the language the fixture's own data declares. Go, Java and Rust come out fine. The language should come from the fixture's data, falling back to the file name only when the data doesn't give one.

subject: fix: MCP server hang under concurrent SQLite write contention (#363)
prompt: Under concurrent use, with several agents and hooks writing learned co-activation data to a project's SQLite store under .neuralmind/ at once, NeuralMind's MCP tool calls hang and the whole MCP process stops responding while one call waits on the database. Writes also fail with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` after only about five seconds of waiting. A tool call blocked on the database shouldn't freeze the rest of the MCP process. Access to that store should wait up to 30 seconds for a lock (a SQLite busy timeout of 30000 ms) before giving up.

subject: fix(synapses): stop decay() compounding on every call (#422) (#536)
prompt: The learned association weights between code nodes collapse much faster than their half-life says. Weakening is supposed to depend on the wall-clock time since an edge was last used, but the SessionStart hook runs the weakening pass once per session, and each pass charges an idle edge its full age again, so after a few sessions edges sit at the long-term floor or get pruned. Running the pass several times over a span (for example at days 10, 20, 30, 30 and 30 after an edge was formed) should leave both the co-activation edge weights and the transition weights where a single pass at day 30 would. Also, the client wrapper's call that takes a list of node ids to mark inactive silently does nothing, because it passes the list where a timestamp belongs. It should weaken every edge touching each of those nodes and return the number of distinct nodes it handled, so a node listed twice counts once.

subject: fix(tier2): exact renewal window, and a runbook step that could not run
prompt: `neuralmind license expiring --within N` stretches its window by up to a day. With --within 60 it lists a customer whose licence expires in 60 days and 23 hours, and with --within 0 it lists one that expires 23 hours from now, which flips the exit code to 6 (renewals due) when nothing is due. A scheduler routes on that exit code, so the window has to be exact. With --within 60, licences expiring in exactly 60 days or in 59 days 23 hours should be listed, but not one 60 days 23 hours out. With --within 0, nothing in the future should be listed or counted as needing attention. The days-remaining number shown for each entry can stay truncated.

subject: fix(mcp): refuse a policy file that doesn't parse, and an empty security or roles key (#586)
prompt: A `security:` role policy in neuralmind-backend.yaml that NeuralMind can't use silently falls back to the built-in role policy, and under that policy a caller that declares role admin reaches every MCP tool. This happens when the file doesn't parse (for example `security:\n  roles:\n    builder: [neuralmind_stats` with the list left unclosed), when it parses to something that isn't a mapping (`- security`), when `security:` is present but empty, and when `roles:` is present but empty because every entry under it is commented out. In all of these cases every MCP tool call should be refused with code security_denied, reason config, and an error that says "Refusing MCP calls". A file that doesn't parse and only mentions a security setting in a YAML comment (such as `backend: [turbovec` plus `# security is configured elsewhere`, `# roles live in another file` or `# identity: os is set on the server`) should still be treated as naming no policy: it is ignored and the default identity settings apply. The health-check subcommand's security-policy check should also FAIL for a role policy the MCP tools would refuse, saying "security.roles is empty", "security.roles must map ..." or "does not parse" as appropriate.

subject: fix(audit): reject records without a hash once the chain has started (#581)
prompt: The subcommand that checks the hash-chained event log's integrity passes logs it should fail: once the chain has started, a record with no sha256 is accepted as a legacy line (an edited last record with its hash stripped, a stripped suffix of records, or a forged record appended without a hash, even with valid records appended after it), a stored prev_sha256 that is altered or missing is never compared, and lines it can't read (not valid JSON, JSON that isn't an object, invalid UTF-8, or longer than the 1 MB line limit) are skipped. Each of these should fail with ok false, first_bad_line set to the physical line number in the file (blank lines count), and a reason containing "no sha256", "prev_sha256", "isn't valid JSON", "isn't a JSON object", "isn't valid UTF-8" or "1 MB" as appropriate; the command should then exit 1 with an error on stderr naming the line ("line 3") and the reason, while search and export keep tolerating unreadable lines. Records written before the chain began should still pass, counted in an `unchained` field next to `total`. After rotation, the continuation marker at the top of the new log chains to all zeros, when it should carry the archive's last sha256 as its prev_sha256 so that the integrity check passes and reports `continues_from` (the archive's file name) and `archive_checked` true. A marker that doesn't match the archive should fail with a reason containing "doesn't match the last hash", a log whose archive has been pruned should still pass with archive_checked false, and a malformed marker should fail with a reason mentioning the "rotation marker" instead of raising an exception.

subject: fix(mcp): apply security.roles and security.rate_limit from neuralmind-backend.yaml (#573)
prompt: The `security.roles` and `security.rate_limit` settings in a project's neuralmind-backend.yaml have no effect on MCP tool calls: the built-in role policy and a limit of 60 calls per minute always apply. For example, with `security:\n  roles:\n    builder: [neuralmind_stats]`, a caller that declares role admin still gets neuralmind_stats, although the Security Guide says leaving admin out of security.roles denies it. That call should come back with code security_denied and reason rbac, while a call with no role (builder) still works. Likewise, with `rate_limit: {max_calls: 1, window_seconds: 60}`, a second call from the same actor within the minute should be refused with code security_denied and reason rate_limit.

subject: fix(compliance): let documentation show an annotation without becoming evidence
prompt: `neuralmind compliance .` reports every worked example of an annotation in docs, docstrings, help text and tests as real evidence, and all of them flow into the controls export we hand to auditors: on our repo, 25 of the 37 annotations it reports are just examples showing the syntax. There's no way to mark one as an example. A `neuralmind:example` marker on the same line as an annotation should drop that annotation and leave other lines alone, including every id of a comma list such as `**SOC 2 Controls:** CC3.1, CC8.1, A1.1` on that line. `neuralmind:example-file` anywhere in a file's text should drop every annotation in it.

subject: fix(licensing): DeepSeek QA critical + high fixes
prompt: After revoking a customer's Team license with `neuralmind license revoke --customer Acme --reason non-payment`, running `neuralmind license renew --customer Acme --term 12` renews it anyway and pushes the expiry out again, which brings a revoked license back to life. Renewing a revoked license should be refused with an error saying that the license is revoked, so the operator issues a new one instead.

subject: fix(turbovec): auto-recover from an index no current turbovec build can decode (#443)
prompt: After upgrading turbovec to 1.0.0, `neuralmind build` crashes on every project that already has a turbovec index, because the new turbovec can't decode the old index.tvim file. A corrupted index.tvim crashes it the same way. Instead, the unreadable file should be moved aside as index.tvim.stale, and a normal build (no --force) should re-embed every node into a fresh index, reporting all of them as updated and none as skipped, so search works again. Relatedly, if index.tvim is simply deleted while the rest of the store under .neuralmind/ survives, a normal build skips every node as unchanged and writes an empty index that search returns nothing from. It should re-embed all the nodes into the new index instead.
